blueprint_topic: Management of Care — palliative-care referral and communication during serious stroke
stem: A client with a severe stroke is receiving disease-directed treatment. The family asks why palliative care is being involved during the current hospitalization. Which response by the RN is most accurate?

options.A: Palliative care can be integrated with active stroke treatment to address symptoms, clarify values and goals, and support the client and family as recovery evolves.
options.B: Palliative care is added when the team expects disease-directed treatment and rehabilitation to be withdrawn in favor of comfort-focused care.
options.C: Palliative care is mainly used after prognosis is established to determine whether the client meets criteria for hospice services.
options.D: Palliative care is usually deferred during active recovery because goals-of-care discussions can interfere with rehabilitation planning.

rationale: A is correct. The American Heart Association's 2024 scientific statement on palliative and end-of-life care in stroke states that palliative care should be integrated at every stage of stroke recovery, including from the initial hospitalization, rather than being limited to end-of-life. The AHA also identifies effective communication, symptom management, and understanding patient values and goals as core palliative-care skills and describes support for both patients and families. B is incorrect because palliative care can occur concurrently with disease-directed treatment and does not imply that rehabilitation or life-prolonging care is being withdrawn. C is incorrect because palliative care is broader than hospice eligibility and need not wait until prognosis is finalized. D is incorrect because AHA guidance supports early integration during recovery rather than delaying palliative involvement out of concern that it will conflict with rehabilitation planning.
educational_objective: Recognize that palliative care after severe stroke can be integrated during active treatment from the initial hospitalization to address symptoms, values and goals, communication, and patient-family support throughout recovery.
source_document_title: Palliative and End-of-Life Care in Stroke: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association; Top Things to Know: Palliative and End of Life Care in Stroke
source_version_date: Scientific statement published online December 16, 2024; AHA Professional Heart Daily supporting material updated December 16, 2024; current page rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: AHA Professional Heart Daily — Top Things to Know, items 1 and 2: palliative care should be integrated at every stage of stroke recovery and is not limited to end-of-life; item 7: primary palliative-care skills include effective communication, symptom management, and understanding patient values and goals; item 9: integrate palliative care from the initial hospitalization and throughout recovery; items 1, 5, and 6 describe support for patients and families. Citation links these points to Creutzfeldt et al., Stroke, DOI 10.1161/STR.0000000000000479.
source_claim_supported: Palliative care after stroke can be integrated from the initial hospitalization and throughout recovery while disease-directed care continues; it addresses symptoms, communication, patient values/goals, and patient-family support rather than being restricted to hospice or the final days of life.

correction_summary: Retained the severe-stroke palliative-care construct but rebuilt all alternatives to remove the uniquely long correct answer and simplistic hospice/end-of-life distractors. The revised item tests realistic misconceptions about concurrent disease-directed care, hospice-only framing, prognosis timing, and rehabilitation conflict.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly supported by AHA items 1, 2, 7, and 9 and appropriately framed for RN communication with family.
option_audit.B: Plausible misconception that palliative consultation signals withdrawal of treatment; incorrect because palliative care can be concurrent with active treatment and recovery.
option_audit.C: Plausible hospice-prognosis misconception; incorrect because palliative care is not limited to hospice eligibility or finalized prognosis.
option_audit.D: Plausible rehabilitation-conflict misconception; incorrect because AHA recommends integration from initial hospitalization through recovery.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All alternatives contain comparable explanatory detail; the key is not uniquely identifiable by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel explanations responding to the family's question.
